{"file_path":"<path>","content":"# File-type filtering in ripgrep

This document covers `crates/ignore/src/types.rs` (and its data file
`default_types.rs`), which implements the `-t/--type`, `-T/--type-not`,
`--type-add`, `--type-clear`, and `--type-list` behavior, plus the small
amount of glue in `crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs` and `crates/core/main.rs`
that connects CLI flags to it.

## Representation: `FileTypeDef` and `TypesBuilder`

A file type is just a name paired with a list of glob strings:

```rust
pub struct FileTypeDef {
    name: String,
    globs: Vec<String>,
}
```

There is no separate "type registry" struct — `TypesBuilder` holds the
mutable state while definitions are being assembled:

```rust
pub struct TypesBuilder {
    types: HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>,
    selections: Vec<Selection<()>>,
}
```

`types` maps a name (e.g. `"rust"`) to its `FileTypeDef`. `selections` is
the ordered list of "select"/"negate" requests made against those names,
recorded independently of whether the name currently exists.

`TypesBuilder::new()` starts empty. `add_defaults()` populates `types` from
the `DEFAULT_TYPES` table in `default_types.rs` — a `const` slice of
`(&[&str] names, &[&str] globs)` pairs, kept lexicographically sorted by
convention (there's a comment asking contributors to preserve that and wrap
at 79 columns). A single entry can register more than one name for the same
globs (e.g. `(&["bat", "batch"], &["*.bat"])`), and `add_defaults` just
loops over both axes and calls `add()` for each name/glob pair.

`add(name, glob)` requires `name` to be non-empty and consist only of
Unicode letters/numbers (`name == "all"` is explicitly rejected because
`"all"` is a reserved meta-selector — see below); it appends `glob` to the
`FileTypeDef` for that name, creating the entry via `HashMap::entry` if
needed. `add_def(spec)` is the string-oriented form used to parse
`--type-add` values, and accepts two shapes split on `:`:

- `name:glob` — a plain association, e.g. `"foo:*.foo"`.
- `name:include:other1,other2` — copies every glob currently registered
  under `other1`, `other2`, ... into `name`. The include list is validated
  up front (`types.contains_key` for every referenced name) so that a bad
  reference fails atomically before anything is mutated; `test_invalid_defs`
  in `types.rs` asserts that a rejected `add_def` call leaves
  `definitions()` unchanged.

`select(name)` and `negate(name)` push `Selection::Select`/`Selection::Negate`
onto `selections`. Both special-case `name == "all"`: instead of pushing one
selection, they push one per key currently in `types`, which is why
`--type all` must run after all `--type-add`/defaults have been applied —
it snapshots whatever type names exist *at the time it's called*.
`clear(name)` just removes an entry from `types`; it does not touch
`selections`, so a later `select`/`negate` referencing a cleared name will
fail at build time (see below).

## Building a matcher: `Types`

`TypesBuilder::build()` turns the builder into an immutable `Types`:

```rust
pub struct Types {
    defs: Vec<FileTypeDef>,
    selections: Vec<Selection<FileTypeDef>>,
    has_selected: bool,
    glob_to_selection: Vec<(usize, usize)>,
    set: GlobSet,
    matches: Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>,
}
```

`build()` walks `self.selections` **in the order they were recorded** and,
for each one, looks up the named `FileTypeDef` in `self.types` (returning
`Error::UnrecognizedFileType` if it's missing — this is where a `select`
against a since-`clear`ed or never-defined name surfaces). Every glob string
in that definition is compiled with `globset::GlobBuilder` (with
`literal_separator(true)`, so `*` does not cross `/`) and added to a single
shared `GlobSetBuilder`. Each compiled glob's position in the resulting
`GlobSet` is recorded in `glob_to_selection` as `(selection_index,
glob_index_within_def)` — this is the join table used at match time to
recover which selection and definition a glob hit belongs to.

`has_selected` is precomputed as "at least one selection is a `Select`, not
just `Negate`s." This drives whitelist-mode semantics.

### Matching a path: `Types::matched`

```rust
pub fn matched<'a, P: AsRef<Path>>(&'a self, path: P, is_dir: bool) -> Match<Glob<'a>>
```

Key behavior, straight from the source:

1. Directories never match (`is_dir` short-circuits to `Match::None`), and
   an empty `GlobSet` (no selections at all) also short-circuits — type
   filtering is purely a file-name concern.
2. Matching is done against the **file name only** (`pathutil::file_name`),
   not the full path. A path with no extractable file name is treated as
   `Match::Ignore` if any selection exists, else `Match::None`.
3. `GlobSet::matches_into` fills a pooled, reused `Vec<usize>` with the
   indices of every glob that matched, **in ascending order of when the
   glob was added** to the set. The code then takes `matches.last()` — the
   last-added matching glob is the "highest precedent" one. Concretely,
   this means when two selections both match a file, whichever `select`/
   `negate`/`add_def` call happened later during `TypesBuilder` construction
   wins. This includes globs within one `include:` definition, since those
   are added in the include list's order.
4. The winning glob's `(isel, _)` looks up `self.selections[isel]`; if that
   selection `is_negated()`, the result is `Match::Ignore`, otherwise
   `Match::Whitelist`. Either way the result carries a `Glob` wrapping a
   reference to the matched `FileTypeDef` (`Glob::file_type_def()` exposes
   it).
5. If nothing matched at all: `Match::Ignore` if `has_selected` (i.e. some
   positive `--type` was requested and this file isn't one of them),
   otherwise `Match::None` (only negations were requested, or no filtering
   at all — a bare `--type-not` shouldn't make everything else disappear
   from `Match::None`'s perspective, since directory walking treats `None`
   as "no opinion").

The `matches: Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>` field exists purely to avoid
allocating a `Vec<usize>` on every call to `matched` (`Types` is cloned per
directory-walker thread, and `matched` is called once per candidate file);
`Pool::get()` reuses buffers instead.

## Where this plugs into the walker

`ignore::types::Types` is not consulted alone — `Ignore::matched` in
`crates/ignore/src/dir.rs` composes it with `-g/--glob` overrides and
gitignore-style rules, in this precedence order (highest first):

1. `overrides` (`-g`/`--iglob`) — an unambiguous match (ignore or
   whitelist) here returns immediately.
2. gitignore-style rules (`.gitignore`, `.ignore`, global/exclude files,
   etc.) — an `Ignore` result returns immediately; a `Whitelist` result is
   remembered but doesn't short-circuit, in case something later reverses it.
3. `self.0.types` — same short-circuit-on-`Ignore`,
   remember-on-`Whitelist` logic.

The final answer is whichever whitelist survived if nothing overrode it
with `Ignore`. This is also documented user-facing in the `-t`/`--type`
flag's long help text in `crates/core/flags/defs.rs`: "this flag has lower
precedence than both the `--glob` flag and any rules found in ignore
files."

## CLI wiring

`crates/core/flags/lowargs.rs` defines `TypeChange` (`Clear`, `Add`,
`Select`, `Negate`), and each of the `Type`, `TypeAdd`, `TypeClear`,
`TypeNot` flag structs in `defs.rs` just pushes the corresponding variant
onto `LowArgs::type_changes`, preserving CLI order. `hiargs.rs::types()`
replays that list against a fresh `TypesBuilder` in order — `add_defaults()`
first, then each `TypeChange` applied via `clear`/`add_def`/`select`/
`negate` — before calling `build()`. `--type-list` (`Mode::Types` in
`main.rs`) simply calls `args.types().definitions()` and prints
`name: glob, glob, ...` for each, sorted by name with each definition's
globs sorted too (both `definitions()` implementations, on `Types` and
`TypesBuilder`, sort before returning — this is unrelated to, and does not
affect, the insertion-order precedence used by `matched()`).

## What a contributor needs to know

- **Adding a default type**: edit `DEFAULT_TYPES` in `default_types.rs`,
  keep it alphabetically sorted and line-wrapped, and prefer reasonably
  popular open formats per the file's own doc comment.
- **Precedence is insertion-order, not specificity**: if you change how
  `select`/`negate`/`add_def` calls are ordered anywhere in the call chain
  (CLI parsing, defaults, includes), you change which glob wins on overlap.
  `matches_into` + `.last()` is the only place this is decided.
- **`clear` doesn't touch `selections`**: clearing a type after it's been
  selected/negated defers the error to `build()`
  (`Error::UnrecognizedFileType`), it does not silently drop the selection.
- **`include:` copies globs by value at `add_def` time**: later `add_def`
  calls that extend the *source* type are not retroactively reflected in
  types that already included it, since `add_def` clones `def.globs` once.
- **Type names are restricted** to Unicode letters/numbers and must not be
  `"all"`, because `"all"` is handled specially by both `select`/`negate`
  (expand to every currently-known name) and would otherwise collide.
- Behavioral changes here should keep the doctests in `types.rs`'s module
  docs and the unit tests at the bottom of the same file (`matched!` macro
  cases) in sync — they're the executable spec for whitelist/negate/include
  interaction.
"}
